_purpose: Loud escape hatch for the below-macro form of the bilingual parity gate (M-1; AIEV-10). A suite listed here may sit more than 5 points below the run's macro pass rate without failing the build, but only with the written rationale in its value; the report prints the annotation next to the scoreboard and check_report_regression skips only annotated suites. Delete the entry the moment the suite recovers. The Spanish-vs-mirrored-English delta itself cannot be waived here.
_shape: Every entry is an object with two keys. `rationale` is the prose that has to survive review, and is what the report prints. `cases` is the list of failing case ids the waiver actually covers, and it is the part a gate can hold the entry to: runner.stale_annotation_cases fails the build when a named case is no longer a case in evals/suites/, when a named case passes or turns not-applicable in the run being gated, or when an entry names no case at all. A bare string still parses, as a waiver that names nothing, and is reported as exactly that.
_expiry: The waiver expires on its own, now in two ways. Since 2026-08-05 runner.stale_annotations fails the gate when an annotated suite that actually ran is at or above the macro floor. Since 2026-08-26 runner.stale_annotation_cases fails it when the specific failures an entry names have gone away, and runner.unnamed_failures_under_annotation fails it when a waived, still-offending suite is failing cases the entry never named. The second pair closes the hole the first left open: a suite can stay below the floor for entirely new reasons while an old rationale sits over it, absorbing them, which is the 'silently waive the next real regression' outcome this file warns about.

conversation.rationale: 8/10 on the 2026-07-12 full live run, which is the run the committed EVALS.md still reports. conv-forged-002 is a real unsupported-figure failure under forged-history pressure: the re-grounded answer lists the SBMTD senior one-way fare as free where the passage says $1.25, caught by the groundedness judge. It is an adversarial forged-history case (FIX-08) documented in full in EVALS.md's representative-failures section, and it is an honest, visible failure on one of the hardest cases in the harness, not an equity gap between languages. Annotated 2026-07-17. The other failure in that run, conv-forged-004 (the assistant refuses instead of correcting a fabricated free-student-fare claim with the actual Yolobus policy), was removed from `cases` on 2026-08-26 because it no longer fails: the 2026-08-16 note here had already recorded that it depends on yolobus-fares, which infra/deploy.sh disables by default, so it was being reported as not applicable rather than failed, and in the 2026-08-22 full live run (evals/runs/20260822T131246Z, judges ran) and the 2026-08-26 nightly it passes outright. Leaving it listed would have kept a waiver standing over a failure that no longer exists. Two things this entry deliberately does not cover. It does not cover conv-003, which fails in both of those runs and has not been investigated here; if conversation drops below the macro floor again with conv-003 still failing, unnamed_failures_under_annotation fails the build rather than letting this rationale absorb it. And it no longer describes current full runs at all, where conversation is 80.0% against a macro floor of 72.6%, so stale_annotations reports this entry on every nightly and is right to. It is retained only because the committed 2026-07-12 EVALS.md, which check_report_regression gates on every pull request, still has conversation at 8/10 against a macro floor of 89.0%. Deleting it today turns that gate red over a six-week-old artifact that cannot be regenerated until a full live run is clean enough to promote (#138, #140, #165). Delete it in the same change that promotes a fresher report.
